This petition coming on for admission this day, th e co  following:
 ORDER 1.

By the present petition the petitioner has challenged the order dated 13.03.2023 passed in MACC No.477/2022 by Ninth MACT, Gwalior whereby the application moved under Order I Rule 10 of the CPC for deleting the name of the petitioner from the array of the claim petition was dismissed.
2. Short facts of the case are that respondent No.1/claimant has moved an application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as Act,1988) for claiming the compensation from the offending vehicle which was driven by driver rashly and negligently and due to negligent act of the driver, the accident occurred and the offending vehicle dashed the electric DP and resultantly short-circuit occurred in the high-tension line and the materials of claimant stored in the cold storage of the applicant was burnt.

Upon the report lodged at Police Station Purani Chhawani,
Gwalior, Crime No.350/2018 was registered against the driver of the truck bearing No.
MH-04-BL-1521 under Section 279 and 427 of the IPC and after completing the investigation,
charge- sheet has been filed.
3. Respondent No.1/claimant has moved a claim petition under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 against the driver of the vehicle, owner of the vehicle and Insurance Company.
However, in the claim petition, he has impleaded the owner of the cold storage(present petitioner) as non-applicant in the claim petition.
The petitioner moved an application for deleting his name and the same has been dismissed by the impugned order dated 13.03.2023.

4. Learned counsel for petitioner submits that as the claim petition has been moved under Section 166 of the Act,1988 the petitioner is neither necessary nor a proper party and no relief can be claimed because petitioner had no connection with the offending vehicle and therefore, the order passed by the claims tribunal is liable to be set aside.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.1/claimant supported the impugned order and submitted that as the material was stored in the cold storage of the petitioner, therefore, he has been impleaded as party in the case and he is a necessary party.

6. Learned counsel appeared on behalf of the Insurance Company submitted that the owner of the cold storage was impleaded in the case, exceeding the scope of the provision of Motor Vehicle Act,
1988 and therefore, the contention of the petitioner is legally correct.

7. Considering the arguments advanced by the rival parties, it appears that an application under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 for compensation was moved in respect of the negligent act of the motor vehicle driver according to the provision the Motor Vehicle Act, which provides that in case of causing any death or bodily injury or damages to any third party as per Section 165 of the Act, 1988 claims tribunal is having jurisdiction to adjudicate the claims arising out of the motor vehicle accidents.
The application under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 may be moved for compensation arising out of an accident of the nature specified in Subsection 1 of Section 165 of the Act, 1988.
As per Section 168 of the Act, 1988, the award may be passed against the driver, owner and insurance company of the vehicle.

In a case arising out of motor accident owner of the cold storage in which the material was stored is neither a proper nor a necessary party and the claims tribunal has committed error in dismissing the application filed on behalf of petitioner under Order I Rule 10 of the CPC.
8. Consequently, the impugned order dated 13.03.2023 is hereby set aside and application moved by the petitioner, Ganpati Cold Storage, is hereby allowed.
9. Respondent No.1 is directed to delete the name of the petitioner from the cause title of the claim petition pending before the claims tribunal.

10. With the aforesaid, the petition stand disposed of.
(VINAY SARAF) JUDGE Vishal Ganpati Cold Storage Through ... vs B M Traders Through Proprietor Bhaskar ...
